name: Sambucus
look_here_first: Start at a stem node: opposite, pinnately compound leaves with serrate leaflets, then a broad terminal cluster of small flowers. Confirm the American elderberry concept from provenance; flower color and leaflet count alone do not separate it from European Sambucus nigra.

project_scope.note: First-pass species anchor; other approved pool concepts remain separate.

genus_diagnostics.leaves: Opposite compound leaves distinguish local elderberries from simple-leaved Viburnum.
genus_diagnostics.flower: Small shallow, usually five-part flowers; the installed close-up shows lobes and stamens.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: Fleshy fruits with multiple pyrenes; dissected fruit photo needed.

study_strategy.warning: Photographed outside Texas; original Commons page identifies Sambucus canadensis. Visually checked shallow lobed flowers and exposed stamens. This flower view does not independently distinguish S. nigra s.s. Leaf/node, whole head, and fruit-stone photos remain needed.

comparison_cards.title: American elderberry and its look-alikes
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Viburnum: simple opposite leaves and usually one stone, versus compound elder leaves and multiple pyrenes. Sambucus nigra s.s.: overlapping heads, dark fruit, and leaflet counts; require documented origin or voucher, not a photo-only confident key. S. cerulea: often waxy blue fruit, but wax can rub off.
comparison_cards.caution: Only one first-pass photo is installed. Missing anatomy is not demonstrated by it.
